answer: Admission requires 3,000 gigabytes of memory-hard computation per identity, which serves as a firm barrier against mass replication. An honest participant completes this labor alone, while 1,000 fakes must incur 3,000,000 gigabytes, creating a cost asymmetry that renders sybil farms unsustainable. The verifier uses a quill to sign the memory pointer trail, checking for any velvet-smooth redundancy in the data access that would reveal a copied process. If any identity produces a fable about its unique computation or attempts to parallelize the work, the verifier triggers a permanent slash.
